# Rule reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run rules`. Edit src/generate/constraints.ts, not this file. -->

19 rules. **Prefers from** is the level at which breaking the rule starts costing a candidate score; **forbids from** is where it becomes a hard veto. See [smoothness.md](smoothness.md) for how the levels work.

## Melodic interval

| Rule | Prefers from | Forbids from | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| `augmented-second` | light | light | Augmented second between adjacent scale degrees (♭6→♮7 in harmonic minor). One scale step but three semitones. Sounds distinctly Middle Eastern; wrong for a singable idiom, and common because the generator reaches for harmonic minor over every dominant. |
| `tritone-leap` | light | light | Melodic tritone. Classically forbidden — the line loses its footing. |
| `seventh-leap` | light | light | Leap of a major or minor seventh. Effectively unsingable. |
| `oversized-leap` | light | light | Leap wider than an octave. |
| `compound-leap` | standard | strict | A leap followed by another leap in the same direction. Fine occasionally when it outlines the chord, tiring when it does not. |
| `wide-leap` | standard | strict | A leap beyond a perfect fourth. Vetoed at the level where the vertical rules begin pushing the line onto chord tones, so it has a counterweight. |
| `leap-beyond-third` | polished | polished | Any motion wider than a major third. At the smoothest setting the line should walk, not jump. |
| `unidiomatic-leap` | light | strict | A leap wider than the instrument comfortably plays. A tenth is nothing on a vibraphone and a real problem on a trombone, so the threshold follows the instrument rather than a fixed number. |

## Tendency tone

| Rule | Prefers from | Forbids from | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unresolved-leading-tone` | standard | strict | The leading tone under a dominant chord must rise to the tonic. Leaving it hanging is the single most audible voice-leading error. |
| `unresolved-seventh` | standard | strict | The seventh of a seventh chord should fall by step. Leaping away from it leaves the dissonance dangling. |
| `unprepared-dissonance` | standard | strict | A non-chord tone arrived at by leap. Dissonance should be approached by step — that is what makes a passing note sound intentional. |

## Motion

| Rule | Prefers from | Forbids from | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| `static-repetition` | strict | never | An immediately repeated note. Not a fault in itself, but once leaps are capped and beats want chord tones, repeating becomes the path of least resistance and the tune stops moving. A preference only — never vetoed. |
| `repeated-note-run` | standard | standard | Three or more identical notes in a row. |

## Melody vs chord

| Rule | Prefers from | Forbids from | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flat-nine` | standard | standard | A melody note a semitone above the chord root, held on a beat. The harshest interval available short of a cluster. |
| `avoid-fourth` | strict | polished | A sustained perfect fourth above the root of a major-quality chord, clashing with its major third. Fine as a passing suspension, muddy when held. |
| `chromatic-tone` | polished | polished | A note outside the prevailing scale. |
| `non-chord-tone-on-strong-beat` | strict | polished | A non-chord tone on a downbeat or half-bar. Restricted to *strong* beats on purpose: forcing a chord tone onto every quarter removes the passing notes that connect a line, and turns the melody into an arpeggio. |

## Melody vs band

| Rule | Prefers from | Forbids from | What it catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| `semitone-clash` | strict | strict | A melody note a semitone or minor ninth from something the band is holding. The most common source of accidental sourness. |
| `parallel-perfects` | strict | polished | Parallel fifths or octaves between melody and bass. Fuses the two lines into one and hollows out the texture. |

## Genre overrides

Genres that disagree with a threshold adjust it rather than forking the table.

### Jazz

| Rule | Prefers from | Forbids from |
|---|---|---|
| `unresolved-leading-tone` | never | never |
| `chromatic-tone` | never | never |
| `unprepared-dissonance` | strict | polished |
| `flat-nine` | polished | polished |
| `parallel-perfects` | polished | never |
| `augmented-second` | light | standard |
| `avoid-fourth` | standard | strict |

### Ambient

| Rule | Prefers from | Forbids from |
|---|---|---|
| `unresolved-leading-tone` | never | never |
| `unresolved-seventh` | polished | never |
| `parallel-perfects` | never | never |
| `avoid-fourth` | never | never |
| `static-repetition` | never | never |
| `repeated-note-run` | polished | never |
| `flat-nine` | polished | never |
